clue.text: Come right, ousted by church record

indicators.note: one thing ousted by another is thrown out and replaced, so the letter for right gives way to the letters for church

parts.note: to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: Someone told to come to the right side is pushed aside by the church, in what sounds like a parish register entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a stored collection of documents, so the word can stand for a record kept for posterity.

clue.text: See 3
Bite is capable of 22

parts.note: if you can do something you are capable of it
the answer at 22 means imitation, and to ape is to imitate

explanation.surface: A small bite described as able to mimic something else.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' points to the answer at 22 across, which suggests mimicking: APE.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury snack served at parties, a mouthful in one bite.

clue.text: Strike dictatorial Sunni movement

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters of the two words being shifted into another order

explanation.surface: A political note on an authoritarian Sunni Muslim faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like part of the politics, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike is the classic form of workers' protest action, the stoppage of labour.

clue.text: Bird feels sad losing wings

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two ends, which are dropped here

parts.note: someone who feels sad about a past act regrets it

explanation.surface: A bird that can no longer fly is understandably sad.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a wading bird of marshes and shores.

clue.text: Oh, very sad — we cut and ran

parts.note: the exclamation oh is written as the letter O

indicators.note: cut here trims the tail off each of the three short words that follow the exclamation

explanation.surface: A sad little confession: someone, very upset, says they cut and ran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of each of 'very', 'sad' and 'we', leaving VER, SA and W. 'ran' looks like part of the fleeing, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business or project is to be in charge of it, the managerial sense of supervised.

clue.text: Jack of all trades can supply jambon

parts.note: jambon is French for ham; read the answer as an instruction, with odd as the signal to rearrange the letters of job man, and it spells this word

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who can provide French ham turns out to be a general handyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer works backwards: an odd arrangement of JOB MAN gives JAMBON.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman doing all kinds of small tasks is called a jack of all trades.

clue.text: Perhaps oral sex, but not giving head in the morning

indicators.note: giving no head here means the word sex loses its first letter

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning

explanation.surface: A risqué line about a bedroom act declined in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is deliberately rude; 'oral' is the kind of test, and 'Perhaps' says it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken test, one kind of examination, so the definition gives an example.

clue.text: Team has true following of stars

indicators.note: following says the word for true comes after the team

parts.note: a side is a sports team
something true is real

explanation.surface: A team whose loyal fans are its genuine following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like a noun for a team's fans, but it is the order signal; 'of stars' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal is the astronomical adjective for the stars, as in sidereal time measured against them.

clue.text: Nothing like slender girls for unscrupulous traffickers

definitions.meaning: the opposite of slender is broad and the opposite of girls is lads, so this describes the phrase literally
dodgy dealers who live by sharp practice

explanation.surface: A seedy gang of traffickers is contrasted with a group of slim young women.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide boy is British slang for a flashy small-time crook or spiv.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a wide boy is a man who makes money by shady dealing, a spiv or petty racketeer.

clue.text: Looking fit, if half unbuttoned

indicators.note: half here keeps only the back five letters of the ten-letter word unbuttoned

explanation.surface: A shirt half undone shows off a well-kept physique.
explanation.definitionFit: Toned describes muscles firmed by exercise, so a toned person is looking fit.

clue.text: In the act (Act II, ii), like Macbeth

definitions.meaning: caught while actually committing a crime
in Act II scene ii of Macbeth the title character returns from murdering Duncan with bloody hands

explanation.surface: A theatre note pointing to a scene and comparing the action to Shakespeare's murderous king.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'act' is the criminal deed; the second is a division of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught with blood on the hands is the idiom for being caught committing a crime; Macbeth literally has bloodied hands after the murder.

clue.text: See 17
Fast food returned without hesitation is still food

indicators.note: returned means what is left of the fast food is sent back the other way
without means the hesitation sound is taken out of the fast food

parts.note: a burger is a typical fast-food item
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A sent-back meal, eaten without pause, is still something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal slang for food of any kind.

clue.text: Representing no certain job scheme, North Sea oil finally switched off

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of each of the seven words before it
switched means the letters of off are changed around

explanation.surface: A union rep complains that a job scheme has gone and North Sea oil has been shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switched' turns OFF into FOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting for someone, as their agent or spokesperson, is representing them.

clue.text: Basic stripping of crude mimes and arty frolics

indicators.note: stripping the three words removes their outer letters, leaving only their insides
frolics suggests the letters of arty playing about into a new order

explanation.surface: A dismissive review of a crude, arty stage show full of mime and silly larking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolics' turns ARTY into TARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudimentary means elementary or undeveloped, the most fundamental level of something.

clue.text: Strange to be upset about blundering courage

indicators.note: about means the upturned word goes round the blundering
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word for strange reads from bottom to top

parts.note: odd means strange
erring is making mistakes, blundering

explanation.surface: It is odd that someone's bungled bravery should cause offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is old-fashioned heroic daring, bold courage in action.

clue.text: Ben's partner was in debt and showed signs of inflation

parts.note: Bill and Ben are the Flowerpot Men of the old BBC children's programme
someone in debt owed money

explanation.surface: A man whose partner fell into debt watched prices rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Ben were puppet flowerpot men in a 1950s British children's TV show. 'inflation' suggests the economy but means swelling up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sails or clouds billowed when they swelled out, showing the signs of being inflated with air.

clue.text: Authorised workplace for Labour today

parts.note: something authorised is official
work gives OP (opus, a work) and place gives POSITION

explanation.surface: An office where the Labour Party is approved to operate.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2015 Labour was the main party not in government in Britain. 'workplace' splits into work (OP) and place (POSITION).
explanation.definitionFit: The largest party out of power in the UK parliament holds a formal role, and at the time that party was Labour.

clue.text: 10 impose love to embrace a given sweetheart

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the impose and love letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: to impose a penalty is to inflict it
something given is granted
the heart of sweet is its middle letter E; the L beside it has no source in the clue, which looks like the setter's slip
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An instruction to force love on someone by holding their darling in an embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter's slip: 'sweetheart' gives only E, so nothing in the clue supplies the L of DELICTO; bloggers agreed. 'to embrace' is the containment signal. '10' refers to the answer at 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means caught in the very act of wrongdoing, which is what the answer at 10 across means too.

clue.text: Refuse to acknowledge noise outside broadcast

indicators.note: outside says the noise surrounds the scattering word

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
to broadcast seed is to sow it by scattering

explanation.surface: Someone denies knowledge of the racket around a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio but here is scattering seed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown a person or thing is to reject any connection with it.

clue.text: The old-fashioned generation's nervous

indicators.note: 's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

explanation.surface: Older people are said to be a jittery lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'old-fashioned' into 'generation's'; the clue has no explicit signal for this, only the possessive suggesting the words own the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on edge is an idiom for being tense and jumpy.

clue.text: Set callback in Adelaide

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the name of the Australian city

explanation.surface: Fixing up a return phone call in South Australia's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue offers two routes: 'callback' gives DIAL turned round, and 'in Adelaide' gives the same four letters written inside the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is a past form of to lay, and laying a table is setting it, so the two verbs match.

clue.text: Model barred from turning on model

indicators.note: barred from means the model's letter is kept out of the arousing word

parts.note: turning someone on is arousing them, giving stimulation
the Model T was the famous early Ford car, so model clues the letter T

explanation.surface: A catwalk model banned for flirting with another model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' appears twice: first as the definition, second as the Ford Model T, giving T.
explanation.definitionFit: A simulation is a working imitation of a real system, which is what a model can be.

clue.text: Pressed four-page ad to be reduced by half

indicators.note: reduced by half keeps only the back half of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A publisher insisted that a four-page advertisement be cut to two pages.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone to act is to urge them, so pressed and urged are synonyms.

clue.text: Protocol book holding up, briefly and audibly, an obstruction to progress for the allies

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the held letters read from bottom to top
holding says the words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A diplomatic rulebook raising an obstacle for the alliance's progress.
explanation.walkthrough: A second route: 'briefly and audibly, an obstruction to progress' is BLOCK shortened, which also sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties allied for a common purpose.

clue.text: Greeting funny girl with wig outside the merry-go-round

indicators.note: outside says the hairpiece wraps around the greeting and the jumbled girl

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of girl are scrambled

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a comical girl in a wig standing by the fairground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' turns GIRL into RLIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirligig is a spinning toy or ride, and the word is an old name for a carousel at a fair.

clue.text: Some of Jordan's water

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A share of the River Jordan's flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A fjord is a long, narrow sea inlet between cliffs, a body of water.

clue.text: See 18
Derailing the work of the armed forces

definitions.text: the work of the armed forces

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: DE is a prefix meaning remove, and a fence is a railing, so removing the railing is de-railing

explanation.surface: Wrecking a train is presented as a military job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derailing' looks like train sabotage, but split it into de- plus railing: taking away a railing.
explanation.definitionFit: Protecting the country is the main job of the military, whose ministry is named for it.
